newsitem.title: USA: Jewish leaders scrap plans for boycott of Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: Jewish leaders scrap plans for boycott of Swiss banks.

text.p: Jewish leaders have scrapped plans to call for a world-wide boycott of Swiss banks because of the establishment of a Holocaust memorial fund by Switzerland's three biggest banks, a World Jewish Congress offical said on Thursday.
"We have gone from confrontation to cooperation," WJC Vice president Kalman Sultanik said.

Sultanik said that a Feb. 14 meeting in New York of the World Jewish Restitution Organisation that was to have discussed a boycott will now be attended by Swiss and U.S. officials and be used to discuss ways of cooperating with Switzerland.

Switzerland's three biggest banks, Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), announced on Wednesday that they would set up a $70 million memorial fund to aid Holocuast victims and invited the Swiss government and central bank to join the fund.

The move capped months of pressure from Jewish groups, joined by the Clinton administration and Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato, who accused Swiss banks of refusing to return millions of dollars deposited by Jews before and during the Second World War.
Decisions still have to be made on how the fund would be administered and who the beneficiaries would be.
